messages:
incident-bot: Pager: HIGH - runtime/gpu-pool reporting repeated OOMs and degraded latency for gen.v2 endpoints. Pager details -> https://incidents.redwood.example/1953001234 :rotating_light:
oncall-amy: On it. Affected customers?
support-lucy: Two customers on prod (cust-omega, cust-nova) saw 5xxs and >2s tail latency, started ~08:20 UTC. I have the support tickets open.
sre-mike: I’m on the host side looking at node-level OOM logs. Suspect GPU memory fragmentation + KV cache retention. Will post logs.
eng-runtime-jay: Pinging in; if it’s KV cache growth we might be hitting pagewalks and eviction thrash. Can we get recent `nvidia-smi` + runtime memstats?
infra-tim: Node list from the affected pool: gpu-a12,gpu-a13,gpu-a14. No recent deploys in last 24h.
eng-ml-alex: Any large-batch traffic spikes? Also need sequence length distribution.
sre-mike: copying logs ->
```
2026-11-02T08:21:04Z runtime ERROR OOM: alloc failed 2147483648 bytes
2026-11-02T08:21:04Z kvcache INFO eviction_scan_start
2026-11-02T08:21:05Z runtime WARN pagewalk latency=360ms
2026-11-02T08:21:06Z model INFO batch_size=32 seq_len_mean=204 seq_len_p95=1890
```
eng-runtime-jay: batch_size=32 + p95 seq_len ~1890 is a red flag. That many tokens in KV cache per request will bloat memory.
product-sarah: Customer impact: cust-omega reported degraded experience on their chat app sessions — intermittent failures. Need ETA for mitigation.
oncall-amy: Short-term mitigation plan: 1) reduce max_batch_size to 8 for gen.v2 routes on affected pool 2) enable aggressive KV eviction policy (evict after 30s instead of 5m) 3) route long-history traffic to fallback model variant (gen.v2-small) 4) restart 1 node at a time if still OOMing. Can infra run changes?
infra-tim: I can apply the max_batch_size change now via runtime flags. Pushing config -> `rctl set pool gpu-pool gen.v2.max_batch_size=8`
sre-mike: Also recommend temporarily disable prefix caching for endpoints with seq_len > 1024. That prevents huge KV entries.
eng-ml-alex: Agree. For safety we should also reduce max_sequence_cache_size to 256k entries.
eng-runtime-jay: Doing a graceful restart plan: drain connections on gpu-a14, restart runtime, watch metrics for 5 minutes, then bring back.
support-lucy: Notifying customers now: "We're investigating increased errors and latency; mitigation actions underway. Will update in 15m"
incident-bot: Config change applied by infra-tim at 08:27 UTC: `gen.v2.max_batch_size=8`
eng-runtime-jay: Patch deployed: prefix cache disabled for seq_len>1024 on pool gpu-pool.
sre-mike: Observing immediate drop in pagewalk latency to ~40ms on gpu-a12 and a13. Memory pressure trending down.
product-sarah: Thanks — customer update sent. Any estimate to fully clear KV cache backlog?
eng-ml-alex: Depends on request churn. With eviction 30s we should reclaim most entries within 1-2 minutes after traffic normalizes. If not, we should force a background eviction sweep.
oncall-amy: Next: monitor for 10m. If OOMs stop, we'll collect memory dumps and logs for RCA. If not, proceed with rolling restarts.
(5 minutes pass)
sre-mike: OOMs still happening but less frequent. Two more OOM events on gpu-a14. Memory graphs attached -> https://logs.redwood.example/1953001234/memgraphs
eng-runtime-jay: gpu-a14 is consistently hitting a high fragmentation metric (frag_ratio=0.78). That node might have stale allocations. Suggest draining and restart.
infra-tim: Draining gpu-a14 now. `kubectl cordon gpu-a14 && kubectl drain gpu-a14 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`
incident-bot: Handoff: On-call Amy -> On-call backup for next shift at 08:50 UTC. (reacted :handshake:)
oncall-amy: I'm going to hand off to SRE Mike after the node restart; I'll remain on thread for context.
(rolling restart executed)
sre-mike: Restart completed for gpu-a14 at 08:42 UTC. No new OOMs observed on that node so far. Overall cluster OOM count dropped 85%.
eng-ml-alex: Can someone grab a `pmap`/heap dump from the runtime process before it re-populates? Need to see KV cache object sizes.
eng-runtime-jay: I collected a heap snapshot at 08:44 UTC and uploaded: https://artifacts.redwood.example/heap/1953001234/snapshot-08-44.json
sre-mike: Snapshot shows many KV entries sized ~48kb with long keys (session histories). Top keys by memory attached in the snapshot. Hypothesis: long chat histories retained per user + large batch coalescing created oversized KV store entries -> fragmentation.
product-sarah: For RCA we need a clear timeline + customer correlation. Lucy, can you link the error timestamps to customer sessions?
support-lucy: Done. cust-omega sessions hitting seq_len >1500 correlate with 08:20-08:28. I attached sample request IDs.
oncall-amy: Logging the mitigation timeline so we don't miss anything: 08:20 first errors; 08:25 infra reduced batch_size; 08:27 prefix cache rules updated; 08:30 eviction policy tightened; 08:42 drained+restarted gpu-a14.
eng-runtime-jay: Additional action: add a soft cap on per-session KV size (reject or truncate histories > 4096 tokens) and return 429 or a truncated response. This would prevent unbounded growth.
eng-ml-alex: We should also add a streaming mode fallback for very long histories to avoid building huge KV entries.
sre-mike: For the postmortem, capture: memory graphs, heap snapshot, batch_size distribution, seq_len histogram, number of active KV entries per node, config change diffs. I'll compile.
product-sarah: Customer impact summary: cust-omega ~2% of calls affected, cust-nova ~0.5%, no data leak, just availability/latency. Escalated to SEs.
eng-runtime-jay: One more data point: `nvidia-smi` on gpu-a14 before restart showed inconsistent free memory vs process allocation (ghost allocations). That matches fragmentation.
infra-tim: We can schedule a kernel upgrade and driver re-init for that node, but that's longer-term.
support-lucy: Customer updates sent: "We applied temporary mitigations (batch cap, eviction policy) and are monitoring. We'll follow up with RCA"
oncall-amy: OK. No active OOMs for last 8 minutes. Switching to RCA collection mode: please upload logs to the incident bundle: https://incidents.redwood.example/1953001234/bundle
eng-ml-alex: Uploading: seq_len histograms, model runtime memtrace, KV eviction logs.
sre-mike: Uploading: dmesg, runtime stderr, heap snapshot link, node memgraphs.
eng-runtime-jay: I'll open a follow-up PR to introduce a per-session KV hard cap + streaming fallback. Tagging eng-runtime and eng-ml.
product-sarah: Timeline + customer impact draft in progress at https://docs.redwood.example/incident-1953001234/draft - please add notes.
oncall-amy: Marking this incident as mitigated at 08:52 UTC. Leaving open for RCA until EOD.
incident-bot: Incident state -> mitigated (08:52 UTC). Severity: P1 -> downgraded to P2 for RCA.
sre-mike: Postmortem action items (short): 1) implement per-session KV cap 2) add seq_len-based routing rules 3) automatic batch-size auto-throttle when seq_len_p95 > 1024 4) node-level defrag investigation with infra.
eng-runtime-jay: I'll own items 1 and 3. Eng-ML Alex will own 2. Infra-Tim will investigate defrag/residual allocations.
product-sarah: I'll handle customer comms and postmortem review with affected accounts.
support-lucy: I'll follow up on tickets and confirm customer satisfaction once RCA published.
oncall-amy: Thanks all. Great triage. Leaving the channel but available in the doc.
(END)
